units.source_text: 他幾乎都不在店裡，總是一大早板著臉匆匆出門，

en.t: He was hardly ever in the shop, and always hurried out first thing in the morning with a stern look on his face,

units.source_text: 只留一位十七八歲的小夥子看守店鋪，這個小夥子當然也負責監視我，

en.t: leaving only a young fellow of seventeen or eighteen to watch the place; naturally, this young fellow was also in charge of keeping an eye on me,

units.source_text: 只要有空，他就跑到外面與鄰居的孩子們一起練習棒球的投接球，

en.t: whenever he had free time, he ran outside and practiced playing catch with the neighborhood children,

units.source_text: 儼然把我這個二樓上的食客當作白痴和瘋子，有時還像大人一樣對我進行一番說教。

en.t: plainly treating me, the boarder upstairs, as an idiot or a madman, and sometimes even lecturing me like an adult.

units.source_text: 由於我生性不會與人爭吵，所以常常表現出一副既像疲憊又像佩服的表情傾聽，並服從他的說教。

en.t: Because I was by nature unable to quarrel with people, I would often listen with an expression that seemed both weary and admiring, and submit to his lectures.

units.source_text: 這小夥子是澀田的私生子，或因一些蹊蹺苦衷，他沒跟澀田以父子相稱。

en.t: This young fellow was Shibuta's illegitimate son, but because of some odd private circumstances, he and Shibuta did not acknowledge each other as father and son.

units.source_text: 澀田一直單身，似乎也與此事有關。

en.t: The fact that Shibuta had remained single all along also seemed to be connected with this.
